That is **Surah Al-Fātiḥah (Chapter 1), verse 1** — the opening verse of the Qur’an (known as the *Basmalah*).

**Arabic text:**
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ

**Common English translation:**
“In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.”

*(Other widely used renderings include: “In the name of God, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful” [Sahih International]; or “In the name of Allah, Most Gracious, Most Merciful” [Yusuf Ali].)*

**Note on numbering:** In the standard Madinah muṣḥaf and most modern editions, this is indeed verse 1 of Surah 1. The verse that follows (1:2) is *Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn* (“All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds”).

**Surah 112 (Al-Ikhlāṣ), verse 1** — note that this surah has only 4 verses total.

**Arabic text:**
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ

**English translation:**
"Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One.'"  
*(Sahih International)*

Or more expansively: "Say: He is Allah, the One and Only." *(Yusuf Ali)*

**Transliteration:** *Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad.*

This is **Āyat al-Kursī** (The Throne Verse), Surah al-Baqarah (2:255).

**Arabic text:**
اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great."

**Arabic text (36:1):**

يس

**English translation:**

"Yā Sīn." (Ya Sin.)

*Note: This is one of the Qur'anic "disjointed letters" (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿah). Its precise meaning is known only to God, though it is traditionally understood as an address to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and an affirmation of the Qur'an's miraculous nature, as the surah immediately continues: "By the wise Qur'an. Indeed you, [O Muhammad], are from among the messengers..." (36:2–3).*

**Surah Al-Ḥujurāt (49:12)**

**Arabic text:**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَّحِيمٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.

Here is **Surah An-Nur (24), verse 35** — the well-known “Verse of Light” (*Āyat an-Nūr*):

**Arabic text:**
اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):
"Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things."

**Surah Al-ʿAṣr (103), verse 2**

**Arabic text:**
إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ

**English translation:**
"Indeed, mankind is in loss,"  
*(or: "Truly, man is in loss.")*

*(Standard translations render it similarly: e.g., Sahih International: "Indeed, mankind is in loss"; Yusuf Ali: "Verily Man is in loss.")*

**Surah Luqman (31:13)**

**Arabic text:**
وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
And [mention, O Muhammad], when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice."

Here is **Surah Al-Mujadilah (58), verse 11**:

**Arabic text:**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انشُزُوا فَانشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Space yourselves' in assemblies, then make space; Allah will make space for you. And when you are told, 'Arise,' then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do."

**Surah Al-‘Ankabut (29:45)**

**Arabic text:**
اتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ ۖ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do."

**Surah Al-Mutaffifin (83:1)**

**Arabic text:**
وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ

**English translation:**
"Woe to those who give less [than due]" — *Sahih International*

(Other common renderings: "Woe to the defrauders" or "Woe to those who deal in fraud.")

The verse condemns those who cheat in weights and measures—giving short measure when they sell, but demanding full measure when they buy.

**Surah Al-Ahqaf (46:9)**

**Arabic text:**
قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًا مِّنَ الرُّسُلِ وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
Say, "I am not something original among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."
